basis: Bacterial infection defined by hemorrhagic manifestations and disordered hemostasis; other organ damage varies.
Dermoid cyst arising in or involving the spinal cord; cutaneous-type contents do not establish skin involvement.
Primary muscle disease; leukoencephalopathy and ataxia each occur in 3/6. Retinopathy 2/7 is below 30%; ophthalmoplegia and dysphagia reflect muscle weakness.
Isolated pituitary GH deficiency; short stature, delayed bone age and reduced muscle mass do not establish additional destructive organ disease.
Glucose transport disorder causing dystonia and other neurologic dysfunction; direct hemolysis with anemia occurs in 4/4 annotated patients, although broader prevalence is uncertain.
Corneal pterygia and digital keloid/fibromatous skin lesions define the syndrome; each is documented in 3/3 patients.
Congenital ocular motility dysfunction; associated neurologic syndromes do not establish common additional neurologic damage across this umbrella.
Storage disease with neurodegeneration; skeletal abnormalities and blindness 80-99%. Hearing loss 80-99% and cardiomyopathy 30-79% omitted by cap; hepatomegaly alone is not dysfunction.
Defined by nervous-system and skin malformations or neoplasms; additional organs vary substantially among subtypes.
Localized cutaneous mucin deposition; no evidence of common extracutaneous disease.
Intellectual disability defines the syndrome; myopia 6/12 and strabismus 4/12 support ocular involvement. Cardiac defects individually <30%; their overlap is unspecified.
Structural abnormal passage involving the urethra, which belongs to the urinary axis.
PRDM16-related isolated cardiomyopathy with ventricular noncompaction and myocardial dysfunction.
Defined congenital structural heart disease, including ventricular septal defect and tetralogy of Fallot.
Skeletal dysplasia, developmental disability and defining obesity (4/6); renal, gastrointestinal and airway anomalies reported in single patients do not establish cohort prevalence.
Nonsyndromic inherited sensorineural hearing loss.
Persistent end-stage kidney dysfunction; renal anemia, mineral-bone disease and cardiovascular complications are separately diagnosed conditions.
Respiratory ciliary dysfunction causes chronic airway disease. Hearing loss is annotated 1-4%; chronic otitis frequency is unspecified. Situs inversus alone is not cardiac damage.
Selective antibody immunodeficiency; recurrent infections do not establish common direct damage to another organ across the group.
Chronic immune-mediated inflammatory polyarthritis of childhood; no common extra-articular damage is established for this group.
Defining craniofacial skeletal malformations; developmental disability 7/19 and urethral hypospadias 4/8 males. Ptosis and proptosis each 5/19 fall below 30%.
GPI-anchor biosynthesis disorder with ID/seizures; skeletal dysplasia/contractures and cataracts 2/2. Chronic lung disease 1/2 omitted by cap; renal echogenicity alone lacks proven dysfunction.
Disseminated TB with defining pulmonary micronodules; granulomatous infection commonly involves liver and spleen/marrow (>30%). CNS and renal damage are less consistently common.
GBA2-related sphingolipid metabolic disease with central and peripheral neurodegeneration. Ocular motor findings and dysphagia are neurologic; skeletal and hearing abnormalities <30%.
Progressive cerebral and cerebellar disease with seizures and profound developmental impairment; dysphagia reflects neurologic dysfunction without demonstrated digestive-organ damage.
